packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 15 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

EXPOSURE NOTE
No outside source was consulted. The images themselves carry modern pencil notes: "X r a" (image-001/002, top
left), "X v a" (image-008/009, top left), a further pencil mark like "Z r a" on an adjoining piece at the right
edge of image-008/010, and a modern cursive note at top right of image-001/003 which I read as "geestelijk
tractaat" (a generic modern description, not an identification of a work). I did not use it to fill any reading.
I have not tried to identify the work or author.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001: overview of one side (pencil "X r a"). image-008: overview of the other side (pencil "X v a").
  Upright orientation. A small piece of parchment, wider than tall (about 20 cm wide by the ruler), written in
  two columns per side. Lower edge is cut through a line of writing in both columns, so text continues beyond
  the fragment; the top margin is present (column tops are the true first lines of each column).
- No running title, no rubric heading, no enlarged or decorated initial. The only articulation is red paraph
  marks (¶) inside the text block: image-001 col. a has two (lines 17 and 24 of the overview count), col. b has
  one at its first line; image-008 col. a has three or four, col. b has at least one faint one.
- No underlining seen, no interlinear glosses, no medieval marginalia seen.
- Script: small cursive bookhand, heavily abbreviated, dark brown/black ink.
- Damage: a horizontal crumpled/abraded band crosses both columns in the upper third and again in the middle,
  with holes; in those bands the ink is rubbed and several lines are unreadable. A second parchment piece is
  attached/overlapping at the right of image-008 with its own writing at an angle; I did not read it (too
  small and foreshortened).
- Tentative interpretation only: continuous prose in short units, each new unit opened by a red paraph and
  words like "Fuit et quidam ..." / "Quidam alius ..."; i.e. a run of short narratives inside a continuous
  text. No lemma/commentary structure is visible.

AREAS SELECTED
- Side "X r a": col. a top (image-002), col. a middle (image-004), col. a bottom (image-006); col. b top
  (image-003), col. b bottom (image-007). Col. b middle (image-005) is mostly rubbed; only fragments given.
- Side "X v a": col. a top (image-009), col. a middle (image-011) and bottom (image-013) in part; col. b top
  (image-010) and bottom (image-014) in part. Col. b middle (image-012) only fragments.
Unread: the crumpled bands on both sides; most of verso col. b; the attached piece at right of image-008.
Images overlap: image-004 lines 1-5 repeat image-002 lines 7-11; image-006 lines 1-3 repeat image-004 lines
13-15; image-007 lines 1-3 repeat image-005 lines 14-16; image-011 lines 1-3 repeat image-009 lines 7-9;
image-013 lines 1-3 repeat image-011 lines 14-16. Repeats are not transcribed twice.

Conventions: ( ) = my expansion of an abbreviation; word? = uncertain reading; [illegible]; [hole].

- Securely read connected stretches: image-006 lines 3-11 (recto col. a foot), image-007 lines 2-10 (recto

  treated as word-spotting, not transcription.
- The crumpled horizontal bands hide roughly 4-6 lines in each column on each side.
- Both columns on both sides are cut at the foot, so the text of col. a does not run directly into col. b;
  the amount lost is not determinable from these images.
- Which side is recto is taken only from the modern pencil "r"/"v"; not otherwise checked.
- Suggested further views: raking or infrared light on the crumpled bands; a flat, straight-on shot of the
  attached piece at the right of image-008, which carries more text in what looks like the same hand.
- This is an unverified image reading.
